summary: Policy-anchored alerts vanish after query-param normalization of route identifiers
description:
Issue summary: After the recent query-param normalization change, certain alerts that are anchored to route identifiers stop firing and become orphaned from tracehook/runbook links. Impact: Customer NovaRetail reports missed alert notifications for production routes; inbound webhook payloads contain a normalized route id that doesn't match tracehook tokens stored on their dashboards, causing runbook links to 404 and PagerDuty suppression in some cases. Environment: prod (us-east), affected org: NovaRetail, multiple projects using route identifiers with legacy suffixes.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Create a dashboard with alert rule scoped to route 'orders:v2-legacy' and enable tracehook linking to include trace_id in webhook payload.
2) Trigger a synthetic spike on that route (POST /v1/infer with header X-Route: orders:v2-legacy).
3) Trigger alert evaluation window until an alert would fire.
4) Observe webhook payload and alert details in Console vs expected tracehook URL.

Expected behavior: Alerts keep tracehook/runbook links intact and webhook payload contains route identifier matching stored tracehook tokens.
Actual behavior: Console normalizes route id to 'orders:v2' during query planning; alert evaluation stores canonical id while tracehook tokens are left with the legacy suffix. Resulting alert metadata does not match stored tracehook anchors, leading to broken runbook links and some outgoing webhook dedup logic treating it as duplicate and suppressing notifications.
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Create dashboard alert scoped to route 'orders:v2-legacy' with tracehook enabled. 2. Generate traffic tagged with X-Route: orders:v2-legacy in prod:us-east. 3. Allow alert window to evaluate; note payload emitted. 4. Compare emitted route id in webhook and the tracehook tokens saved on dashboard (mismatch seen).
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Kapoor (Support): Customer NovaRetail reports that several scheduled alerts didn't escalate overnight. They included runbook links which 404 when clicked. Asked for timelines and sample alert IDs.

2026-03-10 - Marco Liu (SRE): Collected alert-evaluator and tracehook logs. Early hypothesis: query-normalization introduced in platform PR #5892 canonicalizes route ids for evaluation but tracehook store wasn't backfilled. Reproduced in staging with legacy route suffix.

2026-03-11 - Customer (NovaRetail - ops): Provided two failing webhook payloads and dashboard id dash-9082. Confirmed route naming convention changed last week when they migrated internal routing rules.

2026-03-12 - Eng (Query Normalization): Confirmed behavior. Normalization step now strips '-legacy' and '-beta' suffixes for canonical routing. Tracehook tokens are keyed by raw route string. This mismatch can orphan alerts. Suggested mitigation: make alert-evaluator use raw route key OR backfill tracehook keys to canonical form.

2026-03-13 - Support (Aisha): Notified customer that we have a mitigation and ETA for permanent fix. Asked them to confirm if they can accept temporary toggle on their account to preserve legacy route id handling.
investigation_notes:
Initial triage: alert evaluation path normalizes route identifiers during query planning (introduce canonical_route). Tracehook token store uses un-normalized route keys. Two failure modes observed: 1) Alert UI shows canonical id but stored tracehook anchor is still legacy, causing breadcrumb/runbook links to 404. 2) Webhook dedupe uses canonical id and treats mismatched token as duplicate, suppressing some downstream notifications. Reproduced locally by toggling feature flag feature.query_param_normalization=true. Backfill would need to either rename tracehook keys or maintain alias map. No evidence of token loss; tokens are present but under different keys.
Hypothesis: Recent normalization rollout (platform PR #5892) was gated to a subset of services; tracehook indexing job did not include the normalization step, causing the asymmetry.
Observed impact: NovaRetail reported 7 missed P1 notifications between 2026-03-08 and 2026-03-10. Other enterprise customers with legacy route suffixes could be affected.
resolution:
Workaround applied (2026-03-13): Enabled per-org feature flag 'legacy_route_passthrough' for NovaRetail which disables normalization at alert-evaluator for that org; this restored matching between alert metadata and tracehook tokens and unblocked PagerDuty escalations. Permanent fix plan: (1) small patch to alert-evaluator to consult both canonical and raw route keys when resolving tracehook anchors (short-term rollout, ETA 2026-03-17), (2) backfill job to index tracehook tokens with canonical aliases and add alias mapping (long-term, ETA 2026-03-24).
Rollout notes: Patch will be deployed behind feature flag and released to staging for two days before progressive rollout to prod. Backfill job will be run in low-traffic windows with throttling to avoid index thundering.
Follow-ups: Create a task to audit other tokenized stores (saved queries, scheduled-reports) for similar keying mismatches (INT-3301 assigned).
public_response_draft: We identified a mismatch introduced by a recent normalization change that caused alerts anchored to legacy route names to lose tracehook links. We've applied a temporary per-org setting to restore behavior for affected customers and are rolling out a short-term patch and a backfill to permanently resolve the issue. We will follow up with an incident postmortem and notify customers once the fix is scheduled.
next_steps: 1) Merge evaluator patch to consult alias keys (PR ready, reviewers assigned). 2) Schedule tracehook backfill during maintenance window. 3) Run org-wide audit to enumerate route-key collisions. 4) Publish postmortem and update runbooks to include normalization compatibility checklist.
notes_for_engineering: Be careful to preserve token immutability guarantees when writing back canonical aliases. Backfill must be idempotent and include dry-run verification against a sample org. Ensure webhook dedupe logic is updated to consider alias groups to avoid future suppression.
